topic: A small design studio explains why it stopped billing by the hour. Northline Studio is a made-up example.

slides.title: Stop pricing by the hour
slides.subtitle: What changed when our studio switched to one fixed price per project.

slides.title: Hours punish good work
slides.body: The faster we got, the less we earned. A logo that took us 40 hours in our first year took 12 in our fifth, and it was better. Billing by the hour turned experience into a discount.

slides.label: of project time is invisible to clients
slides.note: Research, revisions, file prep and calls. A fixed price covers it. An hourly invoice starts an argument about it.

items.title: Price the outcome
items.text: A rebrand that lifts sales is worth more than the hours behind it.

items.title: Fix the scope in writing
items.text: List every deliverable and round of changes before the first sketch.

items.title: Raise prices every January
items.text: Small yearly steps keep long-term clients on board.

slides.quote: The first fixed quote felt terrifying. The second felt normal. By the tenth, we had stopped tracking hours.
slides.author: Mara Lindqvist

slides.title: One price, one page
slides.caption: Our quotes now fit on a single page: the outcome, the scope and the price.

slides.title: Send your next quote with one price
slides.text: Save this post for your next client call.
